There is a genuine conflict in the evidence regarding whether yoga can increase height. According to high-credibility sources, yoga cannot increase actual skeletal height — particularly after puberty or age 20 — but can improve posture and muscular strength, making a person appear taller [d1][d4][d6]. Greatist explicitly labels the idea that yoga makes you taller a "popular myth," stating "yoga may make you appear taller, but it's not actually making you grow" [d12], and Medical News Today notes that "adults cannot do much to increase their height" but yoga may prevent age-related height loss [d6]. On the other hand, several sources make stronger claims: a yoga master cited by HealthShots asserts that "the practice of yoga is known to increase your growth hormone" and can help adults gain "an extra inch or even a few centimeters" [d2], while Art of Living claims that a relaxed, stress-free mind from yoga "can easily produce the Growth Hormone, which is responsible for the increase in height" [d5]. A trainer cited by NDTV Food similarly claims yoga may help increase height until age 23–24 by activating the pituitary gland [d8], and Arogya Yoga School states from personal experience that "yoga increases height" even after age 21 [d9]. The most credible evidence suggests yoga improves posture and may prevent height loss, but does not increase actual skeletal height [d1][d4][d6][d12].
